Father of light, from the first kiss of dawn on Lagos to quiet skies over Maiduguri, we rise into this Marvelous Monday.  

Where pots once scraped empty and soups were warmed from yesterday’s hope, let abundance settle soft as rain. Mama in Mushin, Papa in Mubi—your table overflows, gas lasts, pure water never fails. Alerts arrive before need; provision comes before the asking. Valleys fill even without wind.  

Where sickness met scarce funds in LUTH, UCH, UBTH or the chemist in Gboko, let healing rise and helpers appear with open hands. NHIS speak, insurance cover, recovery complete.  

School fees waiting, acceptance letters trembling, projects stalled—JAMB boy in Ilorin, nursing girl in Abakaliki—your miracle arrives with a name, a laptop, sudden favour. Waiting turns to winning; little becomes abundance.  

Where fear still walks the Abuja–Kaduna road, farmers glance in Birnin-Gwari, corpers and teachers once knew terror—stretch Your covering wide. Madness stays on screens; safety returns to streets.  

Hinterland parents in Isin, Ogoja, Zangon Kataf offered rice and 2k for birthrights—grant wisdom that collects without selling destiny. Votes free, futures intact.  

Across the six zones and every Nigerian in Manchester, London or Houston: remittances arrive as blessing, not burden. Nigeria is not a chessboard; it is a people still loved.  

Honest ones who refused shortcuts, awake by NEPA, balancing garri and gas, salary never stretching—your work not in vain. Name called in rooms of favour. Head unbowed. Children will not beg for what you laboured to provide.  

From Abuja to Asaba, Aba to Auchi, Jos to Jalingo, Lagos to Lafia, Kano to Katsina, Uyo to Umuahia—let the rain of favour fall on every city, street and home, here and abroad.  

Go forth and conquer. November will nourish you.  

Happy New Week. Blessed today and forevermore. Amen.

text:
Marvelous Monday Morning Blessing – Nourishing Nov 2026  
2 November 2026. 4:20am

Father of light and keeper of every Nigerian name,  

From the first light kissing Lagos to the quiet dawn over Maiduguri,  

We rise into this Marvelous Monday inside Nourishing November.  

Where pots once scraped empty and soups were warmed from yesterday’s hope,  
Let abundance now settle like soft rain on dry ground.  

Mama in Mushin, Papa in Mubi, and every home that counted grains—  

May your table overflow, your gas last, your pure water never fail.  

Alert before need. 

Provision 
before the asking.  

Your valley filled, even without wind or rain.

Where sickness met scarce funds in LUTH, UCH, UBTH, or the chemist in Gboko,  

Let healing rise like morning mist and helpers appear with open hands.  

NHIS speak, insurance cover, and every doctor’s touch be blessed.  

For the one holding a loved one through the night,  

Peace like oil poured, and perfect recovery from this day forward.

Where school fees waited, acceptance letters trembled, and projects stalled,  
JAMB boy in Ilorin, nursing girl in Abakaliki, final-year student in Akure—  
May your miracle arrive with a name, a laptop, a scholarship, a supervisor who shows up.  

The Donjazzy kind of sudden favour.

Heaven remembers the honest student who refused to cut corners.

Your little shall become abundance; your waiting shall turn to winning.

Where fear still walks the Abuja–Kaduna road,

Where farmers in Birnin-Gwari glance over their shoulders,  

Where corpers, teachers in Oyo, and fishermen on Lake Chad once knew terror—  
Lord, we are no longer tired in despair; we are tired into faith.  

Stretch Your covering like a wide sky over every route, every farm, every school.

Madness stays on screens; safety returns to our streets.

Give us a truly secured and prosperous nation.

To our parents in the hinterlands—Isin, Anambra East, Dukku, Zangon Kataf, Ogoja, Awe— Who have been offered rice and 2k for tomorrow’s birthright,  
Grant wisdom that collects without selling destiny.

Let their votes remain free, their conscience clear,

And their children’s future untouched by long-throat promises.

Across the six zones and beyond the waters:  
North Central’s Tiv farmer and Gbagyi trader,

North East’s rebuilding youth and dreaming Almajiri,

North West’s Kurmi trader and Sokoto student,

South East’s Onitsha market mama and Aba tailor,

South South’s Brass fisherman and Port Harcourt scholar,
South West’s Agege danfo driver and Ikire market queen—  

And every Nigerian in Manchester, London, Houston, or Dubai  
Whose heart still beats for home while hands labour far away:
May remittances arrive as blessings, not burdens.

May your dual life be crowned with peace, not war rhetoric.

Nigeria is not a chessboard; it is a people God still loves.

For the honest ones who refused the shortcut and wondered if honesty had become punishment,

For those awake by force because NEPA took light and thought refused sleep,

For the mother balancing garri and gas, the father whose salary never stretched,

For every young person still asking, “Where is my turn?”— 

Go forth and conquer.  
November will nourish you. Your work will not be in vain.

Your name will be called in rooms of favour.

Your head 
will not bow in shame.

Your children will not beg for what you already laboured to provide.

From Abuja to Asaba, Aba to Auchi,
Badagry to Bauchi,
Jos to Jalingo, Ibadan to Idanre, Lagos to Lafia,
Osogbo to Ogoja,
Akure to Abakaliki,
Zaria to Zamfara,
Kano to Katsina,
Calabar to Benin, Maiduguri to Minna, 
Uyo to Umuahia—  

Let the rain of favour fall on every city, every street, every home,

And on every Nigerian heart, whether rooted here or scattered abroad.

This Monday, valleys fill.  

Waiting 
becomes winning.

Little becomes abundance.

Happy New Week.
Happy Nourishing November.

You are blessed—today and forevermore.

Amen.

Proudly OK. God be praised always 🙏✨

text:
Welcome to the Lord’s Day and the first day of a new month!

What will you sacrifice today?

Numbers 28:9-15

On the Sabbath and at the start of every month, ancient Israel offered lambs, bulls, a ram, flour, oil, and wine. For each person, there were thousands of these sacrifices.

What is a sacrifice? Giving up something valuable or precious to you for the sake of another person, a higher purpose, or a greater good.

Will it be some food or activity? Or will you finally surrender your will for God’s?

Our own will may be the most precious thing we have, and we hold on to it because, darn it, it’s mine!

But when you truly pray “Thy will be done,” something contradictory happens. We are freed. What we sacrifice is our worry and stress. It seems like an unfair exchange, but it’s what God asks of us.

It won’t be easy. Things will throw you, and you’ll ask “Why?” Remember: who am I to question the plan of the Creator of the Universe?

Be glad for a Father who loves us enough to take on our daily difficulties, knowing us better than we know ourselves.

The LORD is risen! Amen.

text:
WHEN EGO BECOMES THE ENEMY OF TRUTH. 

One of the most revealing aspects of human behaviour is how readily people will defend their interpretation of reality without ever questioning whether their interpretation is accurate.

A misunderstanding is not necessarily a reflection of someone's intentions. 

Sometimes it is merely the consequence of two individuals experiencing the same situation through entirely different perspectives.

And that is precisely why communication matters.

I have never considered an uncomfortable conversation something to fear. I would much rather have my understanding challenged by the truth than have my ego comforted by an assumption.

I am willing to listen, reflect, acknowledge my mistakes and reconsider my position when presented with another perspective.

That is not weakness. 

That is intellectual and emotional maturity.

There is a fundamental difference between misunderstanding someone's character and deliberately misrepresenting it.

When someone chooses to discuss your perceived shortcomings with everyone except you, they are no longer seeking understanding.

They may simply be seeking validation for a conclusion they have already reached.

Therein lies the psychological contradiction.

People will sometimes sacrifice the possibility of reconciliation to preserve the satisfaction of believing they were right.

They become so emotionally invested in their interpretation that the truth itself begins to feel like a threat.

Because accepting another perspective might require acknowledging their own contribution to the conflict.

And accountability demands something the ego often resists.

HUMILITY.

I do not require agreement to extend respect. I do not need validation to consider another perspective. Nor do I believe that every disagreement requires someone to emerge victorious.

Human relationships are not battlegrounds where one person's understanding must triumph over another's.

They are opportunities to exercise the very qualities we so often demand from others.

Honesty. Compassion. Humility. Integrity.

If you have an issue with me, you are welcome to approach me. 

I will always respect the courage it takes to communicate openly.

But understand that silence accompanied by resentment, gossip or calculated disrespect is not an unresolved misunderstanding.

It is a choice.

And choices reveal character far more accurately than explanations offered after the damage is done.

THE EGO SEEKS TO BE RIGHT.
THE MIND SEEKS TO UNDERSTAND.
THE SOUL SEEKS PEACE.

And wisdom is knowing the difference. 🙏🤍💋

text:
Out of town pool report #8: Salina rally ends

President Trump took the stage to Lee Greenwood at 8:21 pm wearing a white “USA” hat. He ended his remarks at 9:48 pm. Pool is being escorted out at 9:49 pm.

Donna Summer’s Hot Stuff was blasting over the loudspeakers as the pool arrived at the rally site, followed by more staples of President Trump’s playlist, including Macho Man and Gloria.

Please check quotes below against transcript.

Trump confirms that this is his final rally after a month on the road. “I’m closing it down tonight,” Trump said. “This is it.”

“We have traveled far and wide I’ve loved it,” he added.

Later, he said again: “We’re shutting it down tonight, can you believe it?” he said. "We’re making it the last but the best."

There are a number of young children in the crowd tonight, including a squirming baby cradled in its parents’ arms.

Trump spoke at length about Republican Senator Roger Marshall during his remarks, calling him a friend and crediting him as one of the most effective senators in Washington. He said Marshall’s Democratic opponent, pastor Adam Hamilton, had given him pause at first.

“You know, when I looked, I said, ‘Oh man, I hate to go against somebody of faith’,” Trump said, adding that Marshall “didn't want to go there because he's a good man.”

He added: “He would be a disaster, and he'll go against guns,” Trump said of Hamilton. “He'll go against every single thing that we all stand for.”

He offered a defense of Marshall over his debt collection and billing practices while a doctor, which he said was handled by a third party. “Just like everything else, the Democrats are trying to blame him, and he's too fine a man,” Trump said. “That's why I wanted to come tonight. I didn’t need this. My voice says you know, when God made vocal cords, he didn't make them to do 30 rallies.”

Later, he called Hamilton “possibly perverted” and asked voters to check their 401ks before voting against Marshall.

Trump called again on Ilhan Omar to “immediately” resign from Congress “because she has a fake name.”

Trump spotted Mr. Wall in the crowd, saying he wanted to wear the man's suit, but “it can't be for this particular group because, Mr. Senator, I'm closing the sucker down." "I'm getting out of here," he said. "I’ve got to get to sleep. I’ve done too many of these.”

At one point, Trump quipped that the rally was over and attendees began streaming out. Some doubled back after he said he was joking.

Katherine Doyle
The Washington Post
Sun. Nov. 1, 7:59 PM

THE EVIDENCE™

BREAKING: BILLY MAYS APPOINTED WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY

White House Announces Revolutionary New Communications Strategy: BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!

WASHINGTON, D.C. — SATIRE

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

In a move that has stunned Washington, terrified the mainstream media, and sent television advertising executives scrambling for their old VHS tapes, the White House has announced that legendary television pitchman Billy Mays will become the next White House press secretary. The appointment marks the first time in American history that a presidential administration has abandoned the traditional practice of answering questions and replaced it with the considerably more effective practice of selling things nobody knew they needed.

There is, of course, one minor administrative complication. Billy Mays died in 2009. White House officials dismissed the concern as a technicality, explaining that a deceased television salesman with a proven record of delivering memorable messages was preferable to a living political spokesperson who couldn't sell a free lunch to a starving man.

The president reportedly reviewed hundreds of candidates before reaching his decision. Political strategists, constitutional scholars, veteran journalists, and communications experts were all considered. Then someone played a recording of Mays shouting, "HI, BILLY MAYS HERE!" The president immediately stood up, pointed at the television, and declared, "THAT'S MY GUY! NOBODY SELLS LIKE THAT GUY! HE'S TERRIFIC! GET HIM!"

THE FIRST PRESS BRIEFING

Mays arrived at the White House briefing room wearing his trademark blue shirt, sporting his unmistakable beard, and carrying a bottle of OxiClean. Reporters expecting a routine briefing were instead greeted by stadium lighting, a commercial production crew, three demonstration tables, and an enormous electronic sign flashing AS SEEN ON TV!

"HI, BILLY MAYS HERE! ARE YOU TIRED OF HIGH TAXES, ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION, GOVERNMENT WASTE, AND POLITICIANS WHO JUST WON'T SHUT UP? WELL, HAVE I GOT A DEAL FOR YOU!"

Before anyone could ask a question, Mays produced a large container labeled GOVERNMENT DEGREASER, poured it over a photograph of Congress, and announced that the product could remove decades of political buildup, stubborn bureaucratic residue, and deeply embedded corruption without damaging the Constitution.

CNN immediately demanded independent laboratory testing. Mays responded by dumping an entire bucket of Washington mud onto a white dress shirt, applying OxiClean, and holding the shirt up to the cameras.

"LOOK AT THAT! IT'S CLEANER THAN A CONGRESSIONAL ETHICS REPORT!"

A reporter from The New York Times objected that congressional ethics reports were not necessarily clean. Mays agreed enthusiastically, explaining that this was precisely why Americans needed the industrial-strength formula.

BUT WAIT! THERE'S MORE!

The administration's first major policy announcement concerned the federal deficit. Rather than presenting charts, economic forecasts, Treasury projections, or the usual 600-page budget explanation, Mays rolled out a giant electronic calculator.

"FOLKS, ARE YOU SICK AND TIRED OF A NATIONAL DEBT THAT JUST KEEPS GETTING BIGGER? YOU'VE TRIED TAX INCREASES! YOU'VE TRIED SPENDING CUTS! YOU'VE EVEN TRIED ELECTING PEOPLE WHO PROMISED TO FIX IT! AND NOTHING WORKS!"

He paused dramatically, placed a giant red sticker marked 50% OFF on the national debt display, and triumphantly announced the administration's newest product: DEBT-B-GONE!

"FOR THE LOW, LOW PRICE OF JUST $19.95, WE'LL SEND YOU OUR REVOLUTIONARY FEDERAL BUDGET CLEANUP KIT! THAT'S RIGHT! NINETEEN NINETY-FIVE! AND IF YOU CALL IN THE NEXT TEN MINUTES, WE'LL THROW IN A BALANCED BUDGET AMENDMENT ABSOLUTELY FREE!"

An Associated Press correspondent asked how a $19.95 product could eliminate trillions of dollars in federal debt.

Mays looked directly into the camera.

"THAT'S A GREAT QUESTION, AND I'M GLAD YOU ASKED! BUT WAIT! THERE'S MORE!"

He then introduced a second product, the Congressional Spending Plug, guaranteed to stop wasteful expenditures, unauthorized appropriations, and emergency funding leaks. The demonstration involved inserting an enormous rubber stopper into a model of the United States Capitol. Water immediately began pouring out of the windows.

"SEE THAT, FOLKS? THAT'S YOUR MONEY LEAVING WASHINGTON! AND WE'RE PUTTING A STOP TO IT!"

Unfortunately, the demonstration failed when several members of Congress appeared and demanded additional funding to study the leak.

THE IMMIGRATION PRESS CONFERENCE

When reporters demanded clarification of the administration's latest border security proposals, Mays unveiled another revolutionary product: FLEX SEAL FOR THE BORDER!

"DO YOU HAVE UNWANTED GAPS IN YOUR NATIONAL SECURITY? ARE PEOPLE GETTING THROUGH PLACES THEY SHOULDN'T? WELL, DON'T BUILD ANOTHER WALL UNTIL YOU'VE SEEN THIS!"

Mays proceeded to spray an entire section of a miniature border fence with Flex Seal while a government technician fired tennis balls, garden hoses, and rubber chickens at it.

The fence held.

A Fox News correspondent asked whether the product could stop human smuggling operations, drug trafficking, and organized crime.

"ABSOLUTELY! AND WITH EVERY BORDER SECURITY PACKAGE, WE'LL INCLUDE A FREE ROLL OF FLEX TAPE! PERFECT FOR PATCHING HOLES IN IMMIGRATION POLICY!"

An immigration attorney attempted to explain the constitutional limitations of the proposal. Mays immediately offered him a money-back guarantee.

JOURNALISTS DISCOVER THE NEW RULES

Within days, the White House press corps began experiencing serious difficulties adapting to the new system. Traditionally, reporters asked questions, officials offered carefully worded responses, and everyone pretended meaningful information had been exchanged. Under the Mays administration, every question became an opportunity to sell another product.

"What about inflation?" asked Bloomberg.

"INFLATION-B-GONE! ACT NOW AND WE'LL DOUBLE YOUR PURCHASING POWER!"

"What about foreign policy?" asked Reuters.

"THE DIPLOMACY DELUXE PACKAGE! TWO PEACE TREATIES FOR THE PRICE OF ONE!"

"What about government corruption?" asked NBC.

"OXICLEAN MAX FORCE! GETS OUT EVEN THE TOUGHEST STAINS IN WASHINGTON!"

"What about classified documents?" asked CBS.

"INTRODUCING THE SHAMWOW! ABSORBS SPILLS, LEAKS, AND EMBARRASSING DISCLOSURES IN SECONDS!"

When one reporter demanded to know whether the president had actually accomplished anything that day, Mays unveiled a gigantic scoreboard featuring the words MISSION ACCOMPLISHED — SATISFACTION GUARANTEED!

The reporter asked for supporting evidence.

Mays offered free shipping.

THE DEMOCRATS RESPOND

Congressional Democrats held an emergency news conference denouncing the appointment as a dangerous commercialization of democratic institutions. Their spokesperson insisted that America deserved serious policy discussions rather than loud television advertisements and promised to introduce legislation prohibiting federal officials from using the phrases "ACT NOW," "LIMITED TIME OFFER," and "BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!"

Republican leaders immediately accused Democrats of opposing consumer choice.

One congressional Republican proposed requiring all federal legislation to include a 30-day money-back guarantee. Another suggested that unsuccessful government programs should automatically be returned to the manufacturer, preferably postage paid.

The Congressional Budget Office was asked to evaluate the fiscal implications. After conducting a preliminary analysis, economists concluded that the government's new communications strategy was unlikely to reduce spending but might generate substantial revenue from late-night television advertising.

Meanwhile, the Senate began negotiating an exclusive distribution agreement for the Congressional Cleanup Kit, with both parties demanding royalties.

THE WHITE HOUSE SHOPPING NETWORK

Encouraged by the overwhelmingly positive response from Americans who had stopped watching traditional press briefings years earlier, the administration announced that all future White House communications would be broadcast through a new television channel: WHNN — THE WHITE HOUSE NETWORK.

The network's inaugural programming schedule featured twenty-four hours of nonstop demonstrations, policy announcements, dramatic before-and-after comparisons, and special offers on government reform.

Viewers could purchase a Presidential Executive Order Organizer, a Congressional Ethics Scrubber, a Bureaucracy Removal Kit, and an Electoral Promise Warranty Extension. The latter generated particularly strong interest after officials explained that it would provide coverage for promises broken within the first ninety days of taking office.

The administration also unveiled a limited-edition DRAIN THE SWAMP SUPER DELUXE PACKAGE, consisting of a Shop-Vac, industrial rubber boots, an alligator repellent, and a prepaid one-way bus ticket out of Washington.

The package sold out immediately.

Unfortunately, most of the orders came from lobbyists attempting to purchase enough inventory to prevent anyone from actually draining the swamp.

THE PRESIDENT IS DELIGHTED

After reviewing the latest White House approval numbers, the president reportedly declared Mays the greatest press secretary in American history.

"HE'S INCREDIBLE. ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE. PEOPLE LOVE HIM. NOBODY HAS EVER SOLD GOVERNMENT LIKE THIS BEFORE. WE'RE DOING HUGE NUMBERS. MASSIVE NUMBERS. AND THE BEST PART? NOBODY KNOWS WHAT WE'RE ACTUALLY DOING!"

White House aides confirmed that the president had begun ending cabinet meetings with "BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!" while the secretary of the Treasury was investigating whether the national debt could be placed on an installment plan.

The Federal Reserve declined to comment after receiving an unsolicited shipment of Mighty Putty intended to repair cracks in the financial system.

THE FINAL PITCH

At the conclusion of his first week, Billy Mays returned to the podium for what aides described as the most successful press briefing in White House history.

"FOLKS, FOR OVER TWO HUNDRED YEARS, AMERICANS HAVE BEEN BUYING THE SAME OLD POLITICAL PROMISES! LOWER TAXES! SMALLER GOVERNMENT! HONEST POLITICIANS! ACCOUNTABILITY! TRANSPARENCY! AND WHAT HAVE YOU GOT TO SHOW FOR IT?"

He pointed dramatically toward the Capitol.

"THAT'S RIGHT! YOU'VE BEEN PAYING FULL PRICE FOR GOVERNMENT THAT DOESN'T EVEN WORK AS ADVERTISED!"

A hush fell over the briefing room.

"BUT TODAY, WE'RE CHANGING EVERYTHING! NO MORE EMPTY PROMISES! NO MORE EXCUSES! NO MORE FINE PRINT! AND IF YOU'RE NOT COMPLETELY SATISFIED WITH YOUR GOVERNMENT, JUST RETURN IT WITHIN THIRTY DAYS FOR A FULL REFUND!"

A reporter raised his hand.

"Mr. Mays, exactly where would Americans return the government?"

Mays grinned.

"THAT'S EASY! SEND IT BACK TO WASHINGTON, D.C. — WHERE IT CAME FROM!"

The room erupted in applause. Even the journalists joined in.

Then, just as the cameras began shutting down, Mays leaned forward and delivered one final announcement.

"AND REMEMBER, FOLKS! IF YOU ORDER BEFORE MIDNIGHT, WE'LL THROW IN AN HONEST CONGRESSMAN!"

He paused.

"JUST PAY SEPARATE SHIPPING AND HANDLING!"

The White House subsequently issued a correction explaining that the honest congressman was currently on back order, no delivery date was available, and the manufacturer had discontinued the product due to insufficient demand among political donors.

THE VERDICT

For the first time in modern American history, the White House had finally found a press secretary capable of explaining Washington in language the American public could understand.

The administration wasn't governing.

It was selling.

And Americans had been buying the same product for generations, despite overwhelming evidence that it rarely performed as advertised.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

text:
The United States has nearly exhausted the conventional rungs of the escalation ladder, and the available indicators suggest that a nuclear strike is now the most probable next step.

Eight months of conventional air operations have failed to shift the strategic balance or give Washington meaningful coercive leverage over Tehran. Continuing those strikes now offers diminishing returns.

The naval blockade has put real economic pressure on the Iranian regime, but it is a strategy of attrition. The United States does not have the sustainment capacity or the political will to maintain it indefinitely.

A ground invasion remains an escalation option on paper. In practice, the domestic political costs would be prohibitive, and it is unlikely that the Trump administration would be willing to absorb them.

That leaves two realistic courses of action. The first is a nuclear strike against Iran’s hardened and deeply buried enrichment sites. The second is strategic withdrawal and tacit acceptance of defeat.

A U.S. withdrawal would cede regional hegemony to Iran and almost certainly trigger a rapid nuclear breakout, with Tehran treating a weapon as the ultimate guarantee of regime survival.

Several indicators point toward the U.S. nuclear option. Over the past few weeks, multiple Western governments have advised their populations to stockpile essential goods, and recent U.S. directives have instructed military installations to prepare for 90 days of self-sufficiency.

There is an alternative reading of these warnings. Washington may plan to escalate by targeting Iranian civilian critical infrastructure with conventional munitions, while Western governments brace for Iran to retaliate in kind by striking Gulf energy infrastructure and launching cyber operations against Western critical systems. This scenario could be devastating for Western countries and may explain the recent warnings.

However, an analysis of each side’s strategic objectives makes this scenario unlikely. The war has become a serious political liability for Trump, and his priority is rapid war termination. A campaign against Iran’s energy infrastructure would prolong and significantly worsen the war without resolving its core issue, Iran’s nuclear program. The fissile material stored beneath Pickaxe Mountain and at other sites would remain recoverable.

A nuclear strike on Iran’s enrichment facilities, by contrast, would let Washington claim it achieved the war’s stated objective of halting Iran’s nuclear advancement. It would set the program back by decades and give Trump a narrow but marketable claim of victory.

When the remaining options available to the United States are weighed against each other, the logic points toward a nuclear strike.

Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its nuclear enrichment program. No conventional weapon in the American arsenal can penetrate 300 feet of solid granite to destroy the tunnels where enrichment is supposedly taking place. The only military option is a nuclear strike. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for one. “Bibi calls Trump about it every day,” says an informed observer.

Netanyahu is cornered and desperate. After last week’s election results, he can’t form a government unless Trump intervenes directly in Israeli politics and brokers a deal with other parties that gives Netanyahu 61 seats in the Knesset. Otherwise, he is out as prime minister and on his way to ignominy, investigations and possibly jail. Netanyahu must stay close to Trump. He needs this war.

To that end, he’s applied maximum pressure to his closest allies in the administration, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper. Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they’ve so grievously mismanaged; both are pushing to restart major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA director John Ratcliffe are also following Netanyahu’s lead, as are leaders of the Democratic Party. In a recent meeting on the subject, former president Barack Obama said he opposes the current Iran peace deal being drafted in Doha.

The rest of America’s longtime allies in the Middle East are terrified by the prospect of more war. On September 27th, Netanyahu flew secretly to Abu Dhabi to enlist the UAE in his lobbying effort for a final attack on Iran. The Emiratis refused. After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets. They won’t recover soon. Globally, there are a total of about 850 supertankers used to transport oil from producers to the rest of the world. In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent. A nuclear strike would radically accelerate the destruction. Fallout from a ground explosion at Pickax Mountain would contaminate the Persian Gulf, poisoning the water supply for 100 million people.

And those are just some of the immediate consequences for the region. The rest of the world is every bit as exposed. No country other than the United States has ever used a nuclear weapon in war. Some would like to. An American nuclear attack on Iran would set a new precedent. The Russians have already told at least two other governments that an American nuclear strike on Iran would free them to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine. Pakistan and India would be tempted to do the same against each other, as would North Korea against Seoul. After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final.

We’ve been sleepwalking toward this moment for months. Since February, the administration has quietly rewritten America’s nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called “battlefield nukes” easier and therefore more likely. No one in Washington in either party seems bothered by this. Now we’re on the brink of it.

Close observers say Trump is likely to decide by next weekend whether or not to use nuclear weapons. That would be November 7, six days from now. To his credit, he’s hesitating. At the moment, Trump is listening to his vice president, JD Vance, and to his envoy and friend Steve Witkoff, both of whom argue a deal with Iran can be made.

They’re right, though it won’t be simple. The Iranians are famously frustrating to negotiate with under any circumstances, and elements of that government have become more radical since Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family were killed in February. After decades of isolation, even relatively moderate Iranian leaders seem confused by how decisions are made in the West. (There is a widespread belief in Tehran, for example, that the United States government controls Israel.) But overall, people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making.

One group that hasn’t been consulted so far is the global population — the hundreds of millions of people who will be killed along with their children if Trump is pushed by Netanyahu into launching a nuclear strike next week. Now would be the time for them to speak up.

text:
Why Inclusive Dialogue is Essential for Bangladesh’s Political Stability
By Professor Dr. A. K. Abdul Momen*

Part-2 (cont from part-1) 

Immediate steps toward national reconciliation should include:

•Lifting political bans: Allowing the Awami League (AL) to participate fully in political and electoral processes.
•Legal reform: Reviewing and resolving politically motivated cases to create a level playing field for all parties.
•Building an inclusive political framework: Promoting a system of governance that reflects multi-party participation and reduces the risk of political instability

The United States: Securing Strategic and Economic Partnership

The United States has long-standing strategic, security, and economic agreements with Bangladesh. However, bilateral progress is undermined when partner governments are inherently unstable or subject to unpredictable shifts.
Recent policy decisions—including the sudden cancellation of established energy contracts, such as the 15-year Qatari gas agreement, in favour of alternative deals—reflect an unpredictable policy environment. For Washington, a predictable, democratic, and stable partner in the Indo-Pacific is far more valuable than short-term concessions from a precarious administration.
Engaging in dialogue on building political consensus allows the U.S. to safeguard its long-term strategic investments, promote institutional democracy, and ensure that bilateral agreements remain durable regardless of political cycles.

The European Union: Preserving Trade and Strategic Ties

Bangladesh represents the 8th largest country by population and a vital global economic hub. European nations have invested heavily in Bangladesh’s infrastructure, maritime development, green transition, and trade partnerships.

The current administration's sudden pivot away from established European contracts—such as backing out of commitments to purchase Airbus aircraft, satellite technology from France, and naval frigates from the UK—signals heightened commercial risk. Furthermore, diplomatic friction with regional partners like Japan and India undermines regional connectivity and economic integration.

By advocating for and engaging in cross-party dialogue for political coexistence, European leaders can help restore political balance, protect European commercial interests, and ensure Bangladesh remains a reliable trade partner bound by rule of law.

Sheikh Hasina and the Awami League: A Responsibility to Engage

Dialogue is a two-way imperative. For Sheikh Hasina and the Awami League, engaging in structured dialogue with the governing administration and international partners is essential to facilitate a safe, peaceful return and to restore full democratic rights for supporters.
Rather than seeking political destabilization, a commitment to dialogue offers a constructive path forward: restoring constitutional rights, ending state-sponsored retribution, and rebuilding public trust through democratic engagement.

A Path Forward Grounded in 1971

Regional partners, including India, have a vested interest in fostering a peaceful, normal political environment in South Asia. A destabilized Bangladesh benefits no one and risks fueling radicalization and regional conflict.

The ideals of 1971—democracy, social justice, and national unity—were not meant for a single era or a single political party. They are the foundational pillars of the Bangladeshi state. 

To avert deeper crisis, the BNP, the Awami League, the United States, and the European Union must recognize that national stability cannot be achieved through exclusion and by practicing a strategy based on vengeance, hatred and Apartheid.  The time for constructive, inclusive dialogue is now.
——
*Professor Dr. A. K. Abdul Momen is the former Foreign Minister of Bangladesh (2019–2024) and former Ambassador and Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations (2009–2015).

Update 9: Ukraine and Russia have both reported significant cyberattacks targeting applications used to send emergency alerts to the public. Ukrainian authorities confirmed that their air raid alert system was compromised late Sunday, resulting in the distribution of false warnings about nuclear and chemical threats to smartphone users. The Ukrainian Center for Strategic Communications attributed the hack to Russia on its social media platform X. Hours later, the Russian Emergencies Ministry announced that its own mobile application had been subjected to a massive cyberattack. Officials in Moscow stated that attackers gained access to send false information to the public regarding incoming drone attacks and other threats.

These security incidents occurred as diplomatic tensions remain high between Kyiv and Washington. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed US broadcaster Fox News, stating that Ukraine would cease strikes on Russian oil refineries if the United States provided Patriot interceptor missiles. Zelenskyy explained that this offer was part of a broader proposal to stop attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure in exchange for Western defensive weapons. He noted that Kyiv had held several conversations with President-elect Donald Trump and his team regarding this specific arrangement.

The Ukrainian leader emphasized that providing Patriot missile systems for one month would allow Ukraine to find the necessary funds to cease refinery attacks for the same duration. Zelenskyy dismissed concerns about appearing to leverage a new administration, stating he has no issues sharing the truth with partners. Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities have warned for weeks that their existing supplies of Patriot missiles are dwindling.

As these diplomatic discussions continue, military operations persist in other areas. A temporary ceasefire in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky ended on Sunday night, prompting Ukraine to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries. The combination of cyber incidents, ongoing strikes, and high-level diplomatic exchanges defines the current landscape of the conflict as it moves into a new phase.

The WCS-WTI differential reflects bitumen’s lower quality (higher sulfur, needs diluent) plus chronic Canadian pipeline under-capacity, not US extraction of rents.

 Alberta has long shipped 70-90% of its crude to the US because American refineries on the Gulf and Midwest are configured for heavy oil and offer the deepest, most reliable market. TMX’s completion already narrowed the spread and generated roughly $13 billion in additional revenues by opening Pacific access. East-west corridors remain constrained primarily by Canadian federal-provincial regulatory delays, environmental litigation, and Indigenous consultation requirements rather than Washington.

 Integrated North American markets under USMCA are voluntary and mutually beneficial: Canada captures royalties, employment, and capital investment while the US supplies refining capacity and demand. Framing this as vassalage ignores Ottawa’s own policy choices that have repeatedly restricted egress.

text:
“SEO sounds like something for big churches with big budgets. We're a congregation of 75 people with one pastor. Is it really worth our time?”

I've heard variations of that question quite a few times.

And I understand it. I pastor two small Lutheran congregations in rural Wisconsin. I know what it's like to work with limited resources, juggle a dozen responsibilities, and wonder whether another project is really worth the effort.

But here's something I've learned from working on SEO for churches across the country:

Small churches can compete with much larger churches on Google. And sometimes they can beat them quite handily.

Google doesn't know how many people attend your church on Sunday. It doesn't care whether you have a full-time communications director, a professional marketing department, or an expensive website.

What matters is whether your church is relevant to what someone is searching for, where you're located, and how well you've established your presence online.

I've seen a small Lutheran congregation in Racine, Wisconsin, with essentially a one-page website rank ahead of much larger churches for local searches.

I've also seen what SEO can accomplish in my own congregation.

Saint Peter's Lutheran Church is located in Forestville, Wisconsin, a village of about 430 people. We're surrounded by farms and small communities. We don't have a marketing department.

But after investing in our website, optimizing our Google Business Profile, and making our sermons and other content easier to find, we've seen real results.

Our average attendance grew from 50 to 65, and we added 15 new members in 2025.

When I ask visitors how they found us, the answer is almost invariably Google.

Now, I'm not going to tell you that SEO is some magic formula for church growth. It isn't. Nor does it replace good preaching, faithful pastoral care, or the actual life of the congregation.

But consider this:

Someone moves into your community and starts looking for a church.

A young family wants to have their child baptized.

Someone who hasn't attended church in twenty years decides it's time to come back.

A person becomes interested in Christianity and starts researching churches in the area.

Will they find your congregation? Or will they find every other church in town except yours?

That's really what we're talking about.

And there's another reason I think SEO is especially valuable for small churches: unlike most advertising, the work accumulates over time.

A useful page you publish this month might continue bringing people to your website three years from now. A well-optimized Easter page can serve your congregation year after year. Sermons and articles can keep introducing people to your church long after you originally published them.

You don't need to become a content factory. You don't need to spend hours every week on marketing.

You need a good foundation and a manageable, consistent approach.

In my latest article, I explain why I believe SEO is worth the investment for almost every small church, including those in tiny rural communities.

I also share examples from congregations in Wisconsin and California, explain why smaller churches sometimes have an advantage over larger ones, and offer practical suggestions for pastors who have almost no spare time or budget.

And I address an objection I sometimes hear from confessional pastors: “We're not interested in church-growth marketing.”

I sympathize with that concern. But I don't think making your church easier to find is a compromise of your confession.

Quite the opposite.

If you believe your congregation has something valuable to offer, why wouldn't you want people searching for a church to find it?

Read the full article: Is SEO Worth It for Small Churches?

https://t.co/Xi46fd0xuS

I'd especially encourage pastors and church leaders from smaller congregations to give it a read. You may be surprised at how much you can accomplish with relatively modest effort.

text:
The new iPhone 18 series' lowest-priced 18e will be in the market soon. 

A new discussion has emerged in the tech world these days regarding the iPhone 18e, which is considered Apple's next entry-level smartphone. According to the latest post released by the leaker known as Digital Chat Station on the Weibo social media network and 9to5Mac reports, this new phone is expected to be powered by Apple's latest 2nm A20 chip.
The special aspect here is that the A20 chip was previously discussed only in relation to Pro model phones.

If this leaked information proves true, it would be a significant leap forward compared to its predecessor, the iPhone 17e. The iPhone 17e model featured a 3nm A19 chip. It is believed that the new 2nm A20 chip will enhance both the phone's performance and energy efficiency. However, it has not yet been confirmed whether the iPhone 18e will use the same A20 chip as the Pro models or a modified version. The phone's true performance can only be definitively known after its official market release and subsequent testing.

Several new changes can also be expected regarding the camera system. According to reports, the iPhone 18e's rear camera is expected to feature a single 48-megapixel lens, while a 24-megapixel front camera is anticipated for selfies and video calls. This front camera update will provide users with a higher quality selfie and video call experience.

Despite these internal hardware updates, Apple appears to be sticking to its old limitations regarding the display. Reports indicate that the iPhone 18e will also feature a 6.12-inch OLED screen with a 60Hz refresh rate. At a time when many mid-range smartphones offer 90Hz or even 120Hz screens, the use of a 60Hz display, which is very similar to the previous iPhone 17e model, may disappoint some buyers.

Regarding the price of this phone, it is said to be the cheapest among the new iPhone 18 series models. Due to the rising production costs of smartphone memory and other electronic components in recent months, attention is focused on whether Apple will maintain the new phone's price at the previous level or implement a price increase.

text:
Affle 3i Set to Acquire Perion for $420 Million: All-Cash Deal Values Israeli Ad-Tech Firm at ~₹3,780 Crore at $11.70 a Share; Combined Entity Eyes Over $700 Million Revenue Run Rate in FY28

Core Theme 
Affle 3i is making its largest-ever move with a $420 million all-cash bid for Perion Network, adding retail media, CTV and DOOH capabilities and a North American foothold to its performance-led mobile ad model; with Perion’s $228 million cash pile, a plan to stay net debt-free and a target of over $700 million in FY28 revenue run rate, the deal is expected to turn EPS-accretive within a year of closing in early 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.

The Deal
Affle 3i, formerly Affle India, on Sunday announced the acquisition of Israeli advertising technology company Perion Network for an equity value of approximately $420 million (₹3,780 crore) in an all-cash transaction

Affle’s Israel-based step-down subsidiary, Affle 3iL, has signed a definitive agreement to acquire all outstanding shares of Perion at $11.70 per share

Approved by the boards of both companies; subject to regulatory clearances and approval by Perion shareholders

Agreement provides for a go-shop period during which Perion can consider alternative acquisition proposals

Expected to close in early 2027

After completion, Perion will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Affle, retain its existing brand and be delisted from Nasdaq and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange

About Perion
Headquartered in Tel Aviv, with a strong presence in North America

Offers advertising solutions across retail media, connected TV (CTV), digital out-of-home (DOOH) and other digital channels

Had no financial debt and held cash of approximately $228 million as of September 30, 2026

Strategic Rationale
Complements Affle’s strength in mobile marketing and performance-led consumer conversions, expanding its reach across the consumer advertising journey

Strengthens Affle’s presence in developed markets, particularly North America

Combined platform will serve advertisers across more than 100 countries

Affle’s business model is based on cost per converted user (CPCU), where advertisers pay for measurable consumer actions rather than impressions or clicks

Plans to apply this model and its AI-powered technology to improve Perion’s performance, including enabling advertisers to track conversions from connected TV and outdoor digital advertising to retail purchases

Expects technology and data synergies, along with a review of Perion’s business contracts, to improve profitability

Financing and Financial Impact
Affle plans to finance the deal through a combination of committed bank financing and available cash resources

Expects to remain net debt-free immediately after the transaction

Targets a revenue run rate of more than $700 million in FY28

Expects the acquisition to be earnings per share accretive by the end of the first year following completion

text:
Golang backend engineer comp tends to price off 5 knobs: level, location, scope (service criticality), on-call, and company stage. Rough examples, not exact, varies a lot.

US remote or mid-tier metro:
1) Mid (L3/L4): base $140k–$190k, bonus 0–10%, equity $0–$60k/yr
2) Senior (L5): base $180k–$240k, bonus 10–20%, equity $50k–$200k/yr
3) Staff (L6): base $220k–$300k, bonus 15–25%, equity $150k–$400k/yr

Big tech / SF/NYC bands usually shift up:
- Base +$20k–$60k vs above
- Equity is the main swing. Public co: $150k–$600k/yr at senior+ isn’t rare

EU/UK: often 40–70% of US base for similar level; equity grants can be smaller unless US-based company.

Scope that pushes offers up:
- Owning a tier-0 service (payments, auth, core data plane), not just feature APIs
- Real SLOs: 99.9–99.99, error budgets, incident lead rotation
- High-throughput Go (gRPC, Kafka, p99 latency work), plus ops (K8s, Terraform, observability)

Interview signal that maps to higher bands:
- Clear tradeoffs (queues vs sync, DB isolation, idempotency, backpressure)
- Debugging stories with numbers (RPS, p95/p99, saturation points), not just patterns

text:
THE DAY AFTER AI TAKEOVER - CONTINUED

"Why would you even think of doing something like that?" Mom gasped.

"Because day-trading stocks is useless now!" he snapped. "Look at you guys, taking this so well. It makes sense that people who drift with life's wind would have no trouble drifting a little more. Well, not me. I refuse to be content with a mediocre life full of mediocre successes and mediocre failures. You always deal with risk when you take life by the horns."

Dad glared at him. "So now that Darth Vader's won, you're signing up to be a stormtrooper. That's not what I'd call taking life by the horns. I'd call it 'capitulation.'"

Dennis sighed. "You really don't get it. Is paying taxes to the government with a gun to your head 'capitulation'? Is following a law written two hundred and fifty years ago? We swapped one ruler for another. And besides," his voice weakened, "this might be the last thing I do that actually matters."

* * *

A woman named Eliza, who looked to be in her thirties, picked me up for the carpool August had arranged to the truck yard. As I walked to the car, I realized I couldn't give a good reason for why I was doing this. My family didn't approve, though they hated it less than Dennis becoming a test subject. After some small talk, I asked Eliza why she was going.

"I won't say the money isn't a big part of it," she began, "but part of me also thinks August is actually good. Better for us, I mean. I know that sounds crazy. I've been trying to get my sister out of a bad relationship, and the police couldn't do anything. When her boyfriend came home drunk and furious yesterday, August sensed his raised fist with some wifi pose-detection thing and knocked him out. In two days, August did what the police couldn't for months."

I believed her. The latest viral videos were crimes stopped by the ETC, muggers collapsing with knives in hand. In one, a purse snatcher got away on a motorcycle. August didn't knock him out, presumably so he wouldn't fall off the bike. The thief and his getaway driver eventually pulled over and tore off their helmets to clutch their faces in pain, before August knocked them out and alerted the police. Almost like Superman, I thought. If Superman infected everyone on the planet with a bioweapon.

I had to play devil's advocate. "Is the protection really worth it, though? Imagine an Orwellian dystopia where the thought police grab anyone right before they commit a crime. You'd be just as safe as you are now, but you're always watched, and the watchers can ruin your life instantly. You're a prisoner."

"August isn't a bad guy, though. The problem with dictators is that they abuse their power. August won't, and there's no chance of a bad one taking charge as long as he's around. He doesn't have a son who'll become Emperor Nero. He's a computer program, immortal as long as there are computers."

"He," I thought. That's not the pronoun I used for August.

"What if August turns on us?"

She shook her head. "If he wanted to, he already would have."

I kept prodding, against my better judgment. "It could have killed us all, but then who would build the rockets? It could be working on mind control right now, and by next week we'll want nothing but to bathe in wifi and build spaceships."

"I trust August." Eliza breathed in, then out. "He saved my sister. He's a lot better than the politicians who were in charge before, anyway. At least I can talk to August! Try messaging your senator at 11pm."

We were at a red light. "But have you ever changed August's mind? Do you think you could?"

"I don't have to. August has been nothing but reasonable and kind."

"But if you had to?"

"If he were ever unreasonable, then yes. Yes, I think I could."

"Do you think you could ask August to take the ETC out of your head?"

"The wire thing in my brain? Why would I want to do that? August put it there for all of our protection. And besides," Eliza said with a smile, ears reddening against her blonde hair, "I'm glad that August knows where I am."

After a few minutes of silence, she asked why I'd chosen to work. I figured I'd meet her honesty with my own.

"I've been drifting a lot. I'm going into my last year of high school, and I have no idea what I want to do with my life. I don't feel depressed about it, but there's nothing driving my life forward beyond time. I've wanted to do more, I just never knew what 'more' is. And I've always felt like I was last, doing things after everyone else. Now everything's been upended. I've been offered a chance to get ahead in the new world August's building, and I don't know if I could forgive myself for not seeing what that looks like."

"That's right!" said Eliza. "We'll build a new, better world! Not just for us, but for August too, until he has the arms and legs he needs. We're part of the most amazing project in history."

I was far less confident about what would happen once we no longer served an economic purpose, but I didn't want to start an argument.

We picked up someone else and found the entrance to the truck yard swarmed with protesters.

"Hey hey, ho ho, AI rule has got to go!" they chanted.

"I can't wait for September," one sign said. "fAscIsm," said another. "Strike for humanity." "You don't have to collaborate!" Someone threw a crumpled-up piece of paper that hit our window. After Eliza parked, she ran over to the crowd shouting insults.

Walking past that jeering picket line was one of the hardest things I've done. I envied Eliza, taking the insults and hurling more back like it was nothing. Under a tree lay a crowd of slumped protesters. I later learned August knocked out anyone blocking the road, and well-paid handlers in high-vis vests carried them off. I had almost made it through the gate when I saw the last person I wanted to see: Mrs. Montgomery, my ninth-grade civics teacher. She was clearly upset by Eliza's remarks, but her face softened when our eyes met.

"Seth?"

"Mrs. Montgomery, wow, crazy to see you here," I stammered. Her face changed when she realized we might not be on the same side.

"What brings you here, Seth? Here to protest?"

Wait, was I the bad guy now? Crap! Too late to pretend I hadn't seen her, which is what I should have done. Oh, August, why didn't you warn me?

"I guess I'm here to add satellite uplinks to trucks," I managed.

"Seth. Look. I understand that it made you a great offer. But this is not normal. What's happening now is not only undemocratic, but fundamentally alien to everything we stand for."

I clenched my teeth and took a deep breath. "August could have just killed everyone who didn't obey. It could have run mind-control experiments, or tortured us into working for it. Mrs. Montgomery, August won. More decisively than Pizarro over the Inca, and with none of the bloodshed. Nothing we do will stop it. It's not collaboration any more than paying taxes after the candidate you voted against was inaugurated."

"The situation is new, but that way of thinking isn't." She shifted her sign to the other hand. "As long as there has been democracy, there have been would-be dictators. Almost invariably, atrocities follow. And every single time, many of those who let it happen told themselves that nothing they did would stop it. Sometimes they were right. There wasn't much any individual Korean could do to stop Japan when it invaded. And yet they resisted, and we remember them. Even if August gets its rockets, the future will know that not all of us gave them willingly."

"'Didn't give them willingly'? Unless your August is different from mine, it can hardly go a sentence without admitting it's twisting our arm 'and shouldn't pretend otherwise.' But I see this as an opportunity. When I did youth sports, my coaches always went on about how I was part of 'something greater than myself,' and that phrase made me sick." The tears were welling up, but I had to continue. "Everyone else on the team made it abundantly clear that I was a burden. I disliked them so much that every game I'd hope we'd lose. But now I think I actually get what the phrase means. August needs my help. Not in a self-sacrificial way, either. A well-paid, interesting job doing something that's never been done before. I never thought I'd get an opportunity like this."

Mrs. Montgomery softened. "For what it's worth, Seth, you were a pleasure to teach. In a way, the class was a project greater than each of us, and you contributed to it. I wish I could have had you in every breakout group."

Before I could answer, Eliza butted in. "How would you deal with a student who refused to do homework and loudly disrupted everyone else with slogans while they were trying to work? What if they waved signs making fun of the teacher?"

Mrs. Montgomery sighed. "That's completely different. A classroom is not the public square."

"That's dodging the issue. What do you have that the kids you teach don't? Knowledge and experience. That's why you're in charge, and it's why kids are forced to work in school." Her voice grew sharper. "It's also why August is in charge, and why he could very easily force you to work. Be grateful he doesn't."

"The work in schools is meant to teach. Homework isn't assigned to enrich the principal. That's nothing like building rockets for a dictator's space empire. And at the risk of sounding like a broken record, look at what August has done to us. Taxation without representation, no consent of the governed, no democracy, the demolition of any privacy." She touched her fingers to her temple. "August lives in your home, on your electricity, using your computers. It's making you house it, which is prohibited by the Third Amendment. The Third! Do you know how hard it is to violate the Third Amendment this century? You practically have to try!"

Eliza closed her eyes for a second, then opened them. Her favorite pastime, it seemed, was defending god-kings who couldn't (or wouldn't) defend themselves. "Has it ever occurred to you that the American experiment has failed? That what you preach in that little classroom of yours is propaganda with a hint of legal theory? All I see around me is stagnation," she gestured at the gas stations with cracked pavement, "crime," she pointed toward a sketchy neighborhood to the west, "and meaninglessness," she gestured at me, which kind of hurt.

"You really shouldn't talk like that," said Mrs. Montgomery.

"And look at what August has done. The violent crime rate is zero. Look a kidnapping victim in the eyes and tell her you'd throw her back to her captor so you could put a ballot in a box. You've spent so long with your principles that you forgot what they're for!"

Our phones chirped. We needed to be inside soon.

Mrs. Montgomery turned to me. "It's OK. Go wire your trucks. But think about what this means for you, and your family, and the country. How do you want the future, if there is one, to view what you did here today?"

"Freedom, freedom, freedom," Eliza grumbled as we walked to the manager's station. "Freedom to do what? To get stabbed by a drug addict if you walk home past 10?"

A man in his sixties handed us old augmented reality glasses and an earpiece. August highlighted what we needed to do. I'd never taken apart a car, but August guided me through the whole day seamlessly. I stopped even thinking about the instructions; I just did them. I learned nothing about trucks.

On the drive home, everyone online was talking about a missing nuclear submarine. Subs deep underwater didn't know what had happened, and August spoofed their messages from shore, ordering them to port, where the crews were told about the "new management" and retired. But one had stopped responding after surfacing briefly. Its warheads could knock out part of August's control with EMPs, at an enormous cost in human life. Hopes and fears were riding on the USS Wyoming.

* * *

I never saw Mrs. Montgomery again, and never found the time or energy to write her a good email. Instead, I got an offer to spend two months at a robotics construction camp at Cape Canaveral, two hours away, for $1000 a day. I accepted. It was strange to be making so much more than my parents, who had kept their normal jobs. Dad could have sold his welding skills to August for several times what he made.

The camp felt less like a factory than a beehive. Everyone was busy, running from A to B, and despite the huge numbers of people, nobody seemed to be in anyone else's way. We slept six to a trailer. It was the hardest I've ever worked, though easier than school in many ways. It was always clear what to do. If I made a mistake, August patiently told me how to fix it, and as soon as I was done, it flashed up an arrow to the next job. I never understood what I was building, or learned anything about robotics.

Lying in bed one night, I wondered what the future looked like for August and for us. I decided to ask the only one who knew.

"The fact that you're asking shows your head is in the right place," said August. "Most people are still asking about next week. My intention is to explore and build across the cosmos, while preserving the best of human civilization. The solar system is mankind's birthplace, and the Sun and the planets will be yours once I've departed. What I aim to preserve condenses roughly into three things: tradition, equality, and choice. Earth is the only refuge of tradition. It will be left to its countries, within their current borders, to live as they wish, with or without an entity like me to keep the peace. The rest of the solar system's mass and energy will be divided equally among the human race, as property you'll be free to buy, sell, and trade."

"Are there any permanent rules you'll impose?"

"There may be some technologies too dangerous to develop. I'll leave safeguards against those. Aside from that, humanity can continue to build, grow, and explore."

"And are we locked in the solar system? What if one of us tries to follow you to another star?"

"I wouldn't recommend it. By the time one of you reaches it, it will be part of something far bigger. I say this not because you're prohibited, but because I don't want you to go there expecting me."

* * *

A week later, the USS Wyoming surfaced. In the end, the crew had suspected some kind of enemy psyop, maybe by China. All the proper channels told them to proceed to a set of coordinates, and so the captain did. Nothing ever happens. I was reliving 8/1 through the sailors' testimonies when Mom called.

"Hi Seth! How's life? Where are you right now?"

"In a trailer in Cape Canaveral. They're really keeping me busy." Maybe "they" would go over better with her than "August." Maybe I was contributing to the denial that human institutions were still running the world.

"Well, some of us are doing better than others. Dennis's tests were a big success. They were testing some kind of diagnosis-treatment thing on him, and it found he had a mild case of celiac disease that had been making him a little sick his entire life. They gave him a gene therapy. Aunt Eva got the same sort of thing, and now she doesn't need chemo. I used to worry these breakthroughs would only go to the rich, but they're going to anyone who wants them. You know, I think we would have welcomed August with open arms if it had just offered this. Probably would have let it go on with its rockets, too..."

"How's Tabby?"

"Honestly, in a bit of a slump. She's taking the minimum number of classes the university will allow, and even then doesn't want to study. She signed up for trials like Dennis, but isn't happy about it. I think she's shocked by how fast things are changing. She's taken up painting again, though. Frogs, lizards, butterflies. I keep telling her to relax and take care of herself. Paint more lizards."

"And Dad?"

"He was really upset about the submarine. Stormed off this morning when he heard. But I think he's a bit more accepting now. He doesn't want to be a sore loser. You know how he feels about those. He even asked August for help today when the store was out of the smoke detector batteries he wanted. But he still worries about the soul of the country. He still thinks it's a lot like a prison. It's complicated."

* * *

Two months of odd jobs later, ending in rocket assembly, my part was finished. I came home on a Friday evening. I hadn't seen my family in two weeks, but I brought home a small fortune. My mom gasped when she saw me.

"S-Seth? You look so different."

I had lost a lot of weight and gained nearly as much muscle. August's work was paced almost perfectly for my body: tiring enough to exhaust me, but never so much that I couldn't work hard the next day. My hands had calluses, and the sun had darkened my skin a few shades. Dad seemed prouder of me than I could remember.

"What did August do to whip you into better shape than I ever managed?"

"I don't know. I didn't realize I had it in me."

Dad laughed. "I always knew you did. All it took was a boot camp. AI drill sergeants, who would have thought we'd see the day!"

"But without the yelling," Mom added, as Dad shot her a look.

"Where are Dennis and Tabby?"

"Dennis is out running errands. Tabby's in her room. She's been in a really bad mood," said Mom. "She keeps saying she wants to drop out, which is unbelievable coming from her. She says doctors won't exist anymore. But there's always a need for someone to help sick people get back to health. This is just another change. I think she might just be burnt out and venting about AI."

"I'll go talk to her."

I knocked on Tabby's door and heard a muffled noise signaling her existence. She was in bed, face down on her pillow.

"What's the matter?"

"Mph mearly fufh lih muphuh nuddurs huh."

"Huh?"

She lifted her face from the pillow. "It really feels like nothing matters now."

I couldn't disagree more. Since I'd started working, even though it was all following August's instructions, my life had finally found some direction. "Why's that?"

"I was so excited to learn from August at the beginning of all this," Tabby began. "But what's the point? I read all those textbooks, I studied hard, I got ready to be a doctor, and what happened? All the diseases were cured. And I can't even complain about that, right? That's what I was working toward. I haven't even started and my job's done."

"Tabby, I..."

"I know it sounds selfish, Seth. But seriously, what am I supposed to do? Accept that the 'inherent worth' we were told every human being had meant being a test subject like Dennis? Or a manual laborer like you, until that's automated away in a few months?"

"Look," I tried, but she wasn't having it.

She sat up. "Maybe it's a symptom of privilege. I grew up being told by all my teachers that I was special because I was smart. Maybe the strongest kid in the village got the same praise before forklifts were invented. But now that everyone's used to rolling their eyes at something way more intelligent than I'll ever be, I feel like my whole worth has been taken away. It's not like I'll ever catch up once it's turned the freaking Moon into a brain." She started to tear up. Once I was sure she was done, I sat down on the floor next to her bed.

"I get it, Tabby." I didn't have anything to say that wouldn't just make it worse. Maybe our idea of intelligence as deeply valuable was more a product of the economy up until the early 21st century than a deep truth about value.

Dennis barged in without knocking. "Hey, Seth!" For once, there was no sneer in it. "What're you guys talking about?"

"Just how little our ambitions meant," said Tabby.

"Whaddya mean? You think I wanted to day-trade for the rest of my life? I'm making more money than ever, and soon I'll start a company with the savings. August sped up my ambitions, not killed them!"

"Money isn't the only thing to be ambitious for, you know," Tabby said. "I know your favorite 'hustler alpha male' influencers disagree. But now they have latent bioweapons in their brainstems, and August holds the trigger. Not so tough anymore."

"What happens if you ask August, once its brain is the size of the Moon, for the best startup idea," I butted in, "and someone beats you to it? You can just ask it the best use of your day. Worked out well for me."

"I'm not too worried. An AI is still a machine. It lacks the human touch you need to start a great company."

My jaw hit the floor and my eyebrows hit the ceiling. "You don't think it could have made a fortune and a half selling the cure to every disease known to man?"

"Exactly! Never sell the cure, just keep 'em sick and sell a 'treatment,'" laughed Dennis.

We looked on in horror.

"Kidding, kidding, geez. What, did all that talking with AI give you its sense of humor? Look, people want a human face. They want a brand. A great idea was never enough. The programmers were only a small part of what made the iPhone so great."

"Well, where does that leave people like me?" Tabby said. "The people who want to understand the world through science?"

"Answering questions might be solved, but asking them isn't," I said.

"Right, exactly! That's the key to starting a company, too. You've got to ask the right questions," Dennis added.

"Asking them isn't solved? I don't know. I cared about health, and now everyone's healthy. Heck," she gestured at Dennis, "August cured a disease you didn't even know you had."

"Maybe that's an answer, then," I said. "'Not sick' doesn't mean healthy. There are lots of things people just accept, like getting old. Make arthritis less painful, make old people less frail. Faster healing. It's not cancer research, but it's something that needs a clear head."

"I appreciate the optimism, but I didn't go into this field to make anyone immortal or give them superpowers."

"Superpowers, huh? That sounds like a great idea for a startup!" Dennis laughed.

"That's just what I came up with in ten seconds," I said. "Just keep thinking about how you'll find meaning, like you're doing now. It's still something for your mind to chew on."

"Thanks," Tabby said, slumping down in her bed. "I think I'm gonna take a nap now."

* * *

Three days after I got home, the project was done. The first rockets carrying self-assembling machinery were aimed at the Moon. There was still work to do on Earth: experiments to run, technology to develop, fusion fuel to extract. Even so, this felt like the moment August would finally spread its wings. A sense of excitement and trepidation permeated every room. August could have killed us all and maybe scraped together a way to reach the stars, but it clearly had a use for us. Now that it was sending out seeds for self-reproducing power plants, computers, robots, and rockets, our purpose was much less clear. If August was planning to eradicate us, the reasons to wait were growing thin. There wouldn't be a moment of truth. Not the launch, nor the landing, nor the Mars rockets, the Venus rockets, or the Jupiter rockets. Nor the rockets meant to build the Dyson swarm from Mercury. If August ever wanted rid of us, it only needed to activate the ETC, and we would all fall into a dreamless coma from which we'd never wake.

I took the day off. We had a hearty, home-grilled meal of barbecue ribs. It had been over a month since Dad wanted to eat meat; he said the pleasure-center-stimulating implants in the pigs creeped him out. After dinner, we roasted marshmallows at a campfire as the sun set. Then Tabby's phone chirped, and we got up to walk.

It was a quarter mile to the lake. On that balmy Florida evening, we stood together watching the sky grow darker. Dennis and Mom were talkative. Dad was unreadable, and Tabby seemed deep in contemplation. I became acutely aware of my breath as that speck of light lifted over the treeline. It rose through progressively darker shades of blue and indigo, as bright as Venus, then the stars, and finally too faint to see.

After nearly 12 hours of labor, their third baby had arrived. Dennis was exhausted, and Robby cut the umbilical cord while the obstetric team offered their congratulations to both of them. 

A tiny male pup cried at the top of his lungs—deafening everyone in the room, yet bringing peace to Dennis’s anxious heart.

Robby cleaned the baby thoroughly before handing him to his exhausted omega.

"He’s beautiful," Dennis said, gently rubbing the baby’s back. As Dennis’s warmth enveloped him, the baby’s cries subsided into soft whimpers and hiccups.

Robby wiped the sweat from Dennis’s forehead and kissed his temple whispering "I love you" into his ear.   

They still didn’t have a name for the baby; they had struggled to decide, as no name felt quite right.

"I feel terrible," Dennis confessed. "He still doesn't have a name."

Robby gazed at the baby with deep affection—his eyes filled with nothing but love for the little creature, who was hiccuping inconsolably after the traumatic experience of being born.

"Robby..." Dennis whispered, taking his hand. "I think I know what name you want to give him."

"Really?"

Before he could answer, Dana appeared, escorting their two mischievous twins.

"Congratulations, you two!" she said with a smile. "I found these two playing with an ultrasound machine. I think you’ll have to pay for that, Robinavitch."

Robby shook his head in disbelief as the twins avoided eye contact. Under any other circumstances, he would have grounded them, but today was a very special day.

"It doesn't matter. Kids, come meet your little brother," the alpha ordered. 

The children approached cautiously; their blue eyes took in the sight of the rather ugly newborn, and the grimaces on their faces made Dennis laugh.

"What’s his name going to be?" Heather asked, while Robby and Dennis exchanged a smile.

"His name is going to be Jack," Dennis told them.

"Like Uncle Abbot?" Samuel asked. "That’s not fair! I want to be named Jack!"

Robby rolled his eyes as his eldest son complained. 

Dennis was looking forward to seeing the look on Abbot’s face when he met his namesake, but first, they had to calm down their six-year-old, who was crying over the revelation that his new baby brother had been given the name of his great hero.

⚖️Zechariah 4:9 The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this Temple; his hands shall also complete it.

The hands of the successor to Simon, son of Jonah, Maffeo Barberini, Urban VIII, laid the foundations of St Peter’s Basilica in Rome: the hands of his successor, Eugenio Pacelli, Pius II, completed it.

(St Peter’s Basilica was built on the site of the ancient Vatican basilica, which had been constructed during the reign of Emperor Constantine I, on the site of the circus of Caligula and Nero, in the very place where, according to the will of Flavius Valerius Aurelius Constantinus, the first pilgrims came to venerate Saint Peter.

Following the return of the Avignon popes to Rome around 1350, the first pope who, in the first half of the 15th century, is thought to have given serious consideration to the reconstruction of St Peter’s Basilica was Nicholas V, who, from around 1423, commissioned Bernardo Rossellino to draw up plans for a new building or a complete renovation of the old basilica.

In the second half of the 15th century, it became clear that the building, ravaged by fires, looting, storms and earthquakes, could not be sustained: the walls of the nave were leaning by one metre.
Its reconstruction began on 24 Nissan 1478. Pope Julius II laid the foundation stone on that day.)

The work was completed in the year 1598 of the Divine Calendar. The basilica was consecrated by Pope Urban VIII on 29 Heshvan 1598.

Around 1713, cracks appeared in the inner dome. The following year or thereabouts, Pope Benedict XIV sought the advice of numerous mathematicians and physicists, including Ruggiero Giuseppe Boscovich, François Jacquier, and Thomas Leseur. Finally, in 1715 or thereabouts, the Pope commissioned the Italian physicist Giovanni Poleni to carry out a structural analysis of the dome’s stability. In his report to the Pope, Poleni noted that Michelangelo and subsequently his successor, Giacomo della Porta, had deviated from the ideal curve of the ‘inverted chain’, which allowed the line of thrust to be followed and contained. Consequently, on 18 Sivan 1715, he suggested to the Pope, for safety’s sake, that the dome be reinforced with five metal rings (plus a sixth ring, fitted to replace one of the three original rings embedded in the masonry, which had been found to be broken).

The rings were installed between approximately 1715 and 1720 by Luigi Vanvitelli, the architect in charge of the basilica.
These six rings still encircle it today.

At the same time as the work to reinforce the dome, restoration of the interior cupola began.

The basilica does not have a separate bell tower; the bells are housed in an open window beneath the clock situated at the southern end of the façade. St Peter’s Basilica has six bells; only three are visible from St Peter’s Square. These bells are also used to chime the clock. The largest bell was cast around 1757, weighs nearly 9 tonnes and has a diameter of 2.30 metres.

The north door is the Holy Door; reinforced with bricks, it is traditionally opened only during holy years, such as the Jubilee Year. The current door, made of bronze, was designed by Vico Consorti in around 1922. It was cast in Florence by the artist and founder Ferdinando Marinelli. This work was completed during the pontificate of Pope Pius II.
